text: You're free to put your finger in the fire. You're not free to choose not to be burned.
explanation:
Why did God allow sin and death? He placed man in Eden, a word meaning delight, surrounded by love, with no sickness or lack. If He'd made robots there would have been no fall, but no love either. And if He'd secretly overridden Adam's choice, it wouldn't have been a choice at all.

Free choice carries a risk, and man chose rebellion. Choice and consequence come together: "The wages of sin is death." Death was never God's plan for you; Scripture calls it an enemy. That's why Jesus came: to break the consequence we could never undo, "but the gift of God is eternal life."

text: A father rode every Disneyland ride first, to make sure it was right for his little girl. God has gone ahead of you too.
explanation:
When Joseph Prince first took his two-year-old daughter to Disneyland, he queued up for each ride alone first. Some were too dark and frightening; others he knew she'd love. Then he came back and took her on the good ones.

God has gone ahead of you. He made everything else first and man last, so we'd step into a world already prepared. He knows every pitfall on your path. "The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want." It's the sheep's privilege to be led. You don't have to figure out the way; just follow Him.

text: You hate cancer in proportion to how much you love the person it's destroying. That's why God hates sin.
explanation:
Walk past an intensive care ward and hear a stranger's family weeping, and you feel sad, but you have no personal stake. When it's someone you love who has cancer, you hate that disease with a passion, because it's destroying a person you treasure.

God loves sinners. He hates sin to the degree that He loves you, because sin destroys everything beautiful He dreamed for your life. So He didn't just disapprove of it from a distance. He sent His Son to take sin's full penalty in your place and set you free.

text: A sealed tomb, Roman guards, more than five hundred witnesses at once, and apostles who died rather than deny it.
explanation:
Paul says the death, burial and resurrection of Christ are "of first importance." He didn't need witnesses for the crucifixion; everyone knew it happened. For the resurrection he lists them: Peter, the twelve, James, then "over five hundred brethren at once," most of them still alive to be asked. One person can hallucinate; five hundred at one time can't.

The tomb bore the seal of Rome and was guarded by soldiers. Women don't forget where they buried someone a few days before. The authorities could have ended it all by producing a body; they never did. And the apostles went to their deaths preaching it. People don't die for what they know is a hoax.

text: The children solved the giant map puzzle in minutes. On the back was a picture of the king's face.
explanation:
A father gave his children a huge jigsaw map of a country, hoping it would keep them busy for an hour. Twenty minutes later they were back with it finished. How? The back of the puzzle was a portrait of the king. Once they'd assembled his face, the whole country fell into place.

The Bible is full of prophecies, poetry, types and ceremonies that seem scattered when you look at them piece by piece. The Passover lamb, the blood on the doorposts forming a cross, the feasts that fell on the very days Jesus died and rose. See the face of the King in them, and everything fits.

text: "Being justified freely by His grace": present continuous tense. There's never a moment when you're not righteous.
explanation:
Everyone knows verse 23: "All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God." Few quote the very next verse: "being justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus." The word freely, dorean, means without conditions; it's a gift.

You were declared righteous at a point in time when you believed. But here the tense is continuous: you are being justified, constantly, freely. When you're moody, when you've failed, you're still righteous in God's eyes. That's a position of strength from which to deal with the mood: "I'm the righteousness of God; this isn't like me." When the accuser says you're reaping what you sowed last month, produce the receipt. Jesus is risen.

text: "Daddy, why are you angry?" "I'm not angry, darling." Children read God's face in yours.
explanation:
When Jessica was about two, she asked her father why he was angry. He wasn't; that was simply his resting face while his mind was on other things. But long before children understand God, they form their picture of Him from their parents' faces.

So smile at your children. To them, a smile says, "You're approved. You're loved." It's easy to be so absorbed in work and worries that you miss the present, and the present is the only time you have with them. They grow up so fast. "The Lord make His face shine upon you." Let them see His face shining through yours.
